verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splash down off the coast of San Diego" (R1); "splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego" (R2); "splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California" (R3); "splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego" (R4, R6); "splashed down in the Pacific Ocean at 5.07pm PT" (R5); "Splashdown is targeted for 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) off the coast of San Diego" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the exact location of the splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly confirm the date and day as Friday, April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and timezone directly stated in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The splashdown occurred at 5:07 p.m. PDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "5:07 p.m. PDT" (R1, R6, R7); "5:07pm local time" (R3); "5.07pm PT" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and timezone directly confirmed.

verifications.claim: The splashdown ended a 10-day mission around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "approximately 10-day journey around the Moon" (R1); "10-day trip to the moon" (R2); "10-day journey" (R3, R5); "10-day mission" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources describe it as a 10-day mission around the moon.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule carried four astronauts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Four Artemis II astronauts" (R1); "four Artemis II astronauts" (R2, R6); "four astronauts" (R3, R5)

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule endured high-speed re-entry temperatures of nearly 5,000°F.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: "temperatures of about 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit" (R1); "temperatures as high as 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit" (R2); "5,000 degrees Fahrenheit" (R3); "searing temperatures close to 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit" (R4); "temperatures of 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit or more" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Some sources (R2, R3, R4) support nearly 5,000°F, but NASA source (R1) states 3,000°F, creating contradiction.

verifications.claim: Navy divers recovered the Orion capsule.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources mention Navy divers assisting crew extraction and stabilizing capsule (e.g., attaching hardware), but capsule recovery is by ship towing and teams, not divers recovering it.

verifications.claim: The U.S. Navy assisted in recovering the capsule and crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "teams from NASA and the U.S. military will extract the crew" (R1); "Navy divers... helicopters... USS John P. Murtha"; "Navy divers will attach a cable to Orion to tow it" (R2); "U.S. Navy extraction crew" (R5, R6)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm U.S. Navy role in assisting recovery of both crew and capsule.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen" (R1); same names listed (R2, R3, R5, R6)
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew composition listed in all sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is safe.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "all four crew members are doing well"; "feeling great, happy to be home" (R2); "returned safely"; "in good condition" (R3); "all four astronauts... feeling fine"; "all is well" (R5); "hale and hearty"; "four green crewmembers" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Post-splashdown reports consistently confirm crew safety.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission involved a 694,481-mile journey.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Exact distance directly stated, despite minor variations in other contexts.

verifications.claim: Artemis II was the first crewed mission to travel around the moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first crewed mission to travel around the Moon in more than 50 years" (R3); "first humans to travel to the moon and return to Earth safely since the Apollo 17 mission of December 1972" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported; Apollo 17 was 1972, over 50 years to 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew was transported to the USS John P. Murtha for medical evaluations.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "helicopters and deliver them to the USS John P. Murtha. Once aboard, the astronauts will undergo post-mission medical evaluations" (R1); "flown to the flight deck of USS John P. Murtha"; "medical bay" (R2); "helicopter ride to the navy’s recovery ship USS John P Murtha"; "medical bay" (R5); "to a medical bay" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe transport to ship for medical checks.
